question: Should unchanged over-limit GitHub-backed skill display names be grandfathered like hosted publish titles, or should sync intentionally normalize them on the next run?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible product policies, but the current PR changes existing catalog metadata during sync without visible maintainer confirmation of that upgrade behavior.

options.title: Preserve GitHub-backed legacy names
options.body: Before merge, keep unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names grandfathered like hosted titles, or add an explicit tested migration path for renaming them.

options.title: Accept sync renames as policy
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept that GitHub-backed skills are normalized on next sync, but the PR should state that upgrade behavior and add focused tests or proof for it.

options.title: Pause for display-name policy
options.body: If the 40-character maximum or legacy handling is not confirmed, pause this PR until the linked issue records the intended public policy.

recommendation.title: Preserve GitHub-backed legacy names
recommendation.body: Before merge, keep unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names grandfathered like hosted titles, or add an explicit tested migration path for renaming them.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest current-history owner for the publish helper and GitHub-backed sync surfaces affected by this compatibility choice.
